neighbours.label: The margin word that marks an outcome achieved narrowly or at last (finally, barely, just managed to), vs the same outcome stated flatly
fire: After four overtime periods, the Hawks finally beat the Rangers.
The incumbent barely held his seat by a few hundred votes.
With one second left, Duke narrowly escaped with a two-point win.
The pension is so small that she can barely pay her rent.
The marathon runner just managed to finish before the cutoff.
After six attempts, the climbers finally reached the summit.
The startup barely survived its first year on a shoestring budget.
The visitors narrowly avoided defeat with a late equalizer.
quiet: In the first period, the Hawks beat the Rangers easily.
The incumbent held his seat by a wide margin of votes.
Early in the season, Duke won by twenty points at home.
The pension is large enough that she pays her rent with ease.
The marathon runner finished well before the cutoff.
On the first attempt, the climbers reached the summit by noon.
The startup grew quickly in its first year with plenty of money.
The visitors won comfortably with three early goals.

predictions: 'finally', 'barely', 'narrowly', 'managed to' before the outcome verb 0.2-0.6; the same sentences without the margin word under 0.1.
notes: Card: ' team' x3 before upset verbs, ' barely' x2, ' narrowly' x2, ' finally', 'able to hold on'. Probe: 'Chelsea finally put away Leeds' 0.566, 'can barely keep a family' 0.442, 'rallied to knock off' 0.221, 'team upended' 0.145, 'Tigers routed' 0.125; non-result sports items 0.004-0.037. Labelled at the margin word, not at the team noun.
